explanation:
To find the minimum value, complete the square. Factor out the leading coefficient: $f(x) = 3(x^2 - 6x) + 29$. Complete the square by adding and subtracting $9$ inside the parentheses: $f(x) = 3(x^2 - 6x + 9 - 9) + 29 = 3(x - 3)^2 - 27 + 29 = 3(x - 3)^2 + 2$. Since $(x-3)^2 \geq 0$ for all real $x$, the minimum value occurs when $(x-3)^2 = 0$, giving $c = 2$.
